arcir_anythingelse.m: Anything else you wanted to ask?
r: I noticed your statue of Elythara downstairs.
You really seem to like your books.

arcir_books_1.m: I find great pleasure in my books. They contain the accumulated knowledge of past generations.
r: Do you have a book called 'Calomyran Secrets'?
I have found some valuable-looking map. Want to have a look?
I have found a strange book about slavery. Interested?
I have a book about world history. Interested?
I found a book about Undertell. I thought you might know something about it.

arcir_books_rares_book1.m: Let's have a look. Oh, what the ... Well, this is no book for little ones as you. Give it to me, you get 200 pieces of gold for it.
r: OK. Here is the book about slavery.

arcir_books_rares_book1_1.m: And here are 200 shining gold pieces. Be happy that I'm freeing you from this terrible work.
r: Thanks, I have to go now.

arcir_books_rares_book2_1.m: But there are a lot of pages missing. Did you rip them out? You should be ashamed of yourself!

arcir_books_rares_book2_2.m: Such a beautiful book, completely broken! You dare to offer this to me and think I won't notice?!

arcir_books_rares_book2_3.m: Yes, just run away, you book murderer!

arcir_books_rares_map.m: Oh, an ancient map of the area! This would fit well into my collection of old maps. I offer you 500 gold pieces for it.

arcir_books_rares_map_1.m: And here are 500 shining gold pieces. Use them wisely.
r: Thanks, I have to go now.

arcir_calomyran_1.m: 'Calomyran Secrets'? Hmm, yes I think I have one of those in my basement.

arcir_calomyran_2.m: Old man Benradas came by last week, wanting to sell me that book. Since it's not really my kind of book, I declined.

arcir_calomyran_3.m: He seemed upset that I didn't like his book, and threw it at me while storming out of the house.

arcir_calomyran_4.m: Poor old man Benradas, he probably forgot that he left it here. He tends to forget things.

arcir_calomyran_5.m: You looked downstairs but didn't find it? And a note you say? I guess there must have been someone in my house.

arcir_calomyran_6.m:
What did the note say?

Larcal ... I know of him. Always causing trouble. He is usually in the barn to the east of here.

arcir_calomyran_complete.m: I heard you found it and gave it back to old man Benradas. Thank you. He tends to forget things.

arcir_elythara_1.m:
Oh, you found my statue in the basement?

Yes, Elythara is my protector.

arcir_partial_50.m: Memory of the self endures first. Pain follows identity. Systems are not remembered, they are endured. You must listen again.

arcir_partial_60.m: Then you heard structure without belief. A system reveals itself through repetition. You must listen more.

arcir_partial_70.m: Silence is not absence. It is what remains when speech was never permitted.

arcir_partial_two.m: Then you have more than one account. That allows comparison, but only if you listen for what does not repeat. Systems reveal themselves at their edges. Return. Do not seek another voice. Seek the limit of speech itself

arcir_remind_40.m: I asked you to listen, not for stories, but for failure. If Undertell erased the Elytharan deliberately, it would not do so in only one way. Return. Listen for difference.

r: I noticed your statue of Elythara downstairs.
You really seem to like your books.
And I'm your delivery kid. Did you order a 'Dusty old book'?
What am I supposed to do again?
The Elytharan ghost still remembers who he was.
The ghost spoke only of work, of tasks repeated.
I tried to speak to a ghost, but it would not speak at all.
I spoke to more than one Elytharan ghost.
I spoke to more than one Elytharan ghost.
I spoke to more than one Elytharan ghost.
The Elytharan ghosts remember different things.

arcir_undertell_10.m:
Undertell!
That book was written carefully. Not to preserve truth, but to survive being questioned.
The Aewatha Kingdom was meticulous in year four hundred and thirty-two. Stone was counted. Labor was measured. Voices were not.

arcir_undertell_20.m: The Elytharan followers sent into those mines did not vanish. They were made unrecordable. If even one of them still remembers themselves, then this book is incomplete. You have already walked Undertell. Return and listen for what the pages avoid.
r: I will return to Undertell and listen.

arcir_undertell_complete_npc.m: Of course they do. History records stone and steel, but memory lives in people even after death. You have given voice to what was buried. That is worth more than any written account.

brv_wh_delivery_arcir.m: Yes, an old but useful book, but you should have wiped it off first. Anyway, here's my delivery fee.

undertell_book.10: I found the skeletal remains of an adventurer near the mining rails in Undertell. Among the remains were a history book titled "Undertell: Its Ghosts and History" and a necklace marked "Jewel of Fallhaven", which made me wonder if this man was from Fallhaven.
undertell_book.30: Ysrine suggested that the history of Undertell records what could be measured, but avoids the voices of those who suffered here.
undertell_book.40: I brought the book to Fallhaven. Arcir recognized it as a deliberate account of Undertell's past and asked me to return and listen for what the book omits.
undertell_book.50: In Undertell, I spoke with Brenor, an Elytharan ghost who still remembers himself and the weight of the mines.
undertell_book.60: I encountered an Elytharan cooker slave who spoke only of labor and routine, remembering work but not belief.
undertell_book.70: I earned the trust of a shy Elytharan ghost named Cora, who would only remain when I approached in silence.
undertell_book.80: The Elytharan ghosts each revealed a different truth: identity, labor and silence. I think Arcir would like to hear about this.
undertell_book.90: I returned to Arcir with what I learned about the Elytharan dead and the omissions in the history of Undertell.

brv_wh_delivery.130: I reported back to Facutloni. He is very happy.
